bill.officialSummary: This resolution provides for the House of Representatives to consider the following measures: H.J. Res.42, Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to Energy Conservation Program for Appliance Standards: Certification Requirements, Labeling Requirements, and Enforcement Provisions for Certain Consumer Products and Commercial Equipment ; H.J. Res. 61, Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing ; and S.J. Res. 11, Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management relating to Protection of Marine Archaeological Resources . Under the resolution, all points of order against consideration of each measure are waived; the measures shall be considered as read; and all points of order against provisions in the measures are waived. The resolution further provides that the previous question shall be considered as ordered on each measure (and any amendment thereto) to final passage without intervening motion except one hour of debate and one motion to recommit.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution sets the rules for the House to debate and vote on three separate measures that would overturn federal regulations. The three regulations cover energy-efficiency labeling for appliances, air-pollution standards for tire manufacturing, and protections for underwater archaeological sites. The resolution waives procedural objections, allows one hour of debate on each measure, and moves them directly to a final vote.

industries.rationale: The resolution enables consideration of disapproval measures affecting appliance certification and labeling standards as well as emission standards for tire manufacturing.
Appliance labeling and certification requirements directly affect retailers and manufacturers of consumer products.
The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management rule on marine archaeological resources may affect offshore energy operations that encounter protected sites.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
